articleTitle: The Working Principles of ESP32 and Analytical Comparison of using Low-Cost Microcontroller Modules in Embedded Systems Design
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: With the emergence of many low-cost development platforms, designing an embedded system has become more flexible using different microcontroller platforms. However, it is necessary to consider various factors before selecting the brain of embedded systems, the microcontroller. This paper compares two commonly used development boards in designing embedded systems with one of the latest boards manufactured for high-performance, low-cost embedded systems design called ESP32. The comparison is based on hardware specifications, as well as programming tools. A Wi-Fi analyzer system was designed and implemented as an example of using the ESP32 module in low-cost, low-energy embedded systems design. In addition to the ESP32, a Graphical LCD is used in the design as an output device. However, there is a lack of literature on establishing serial communication between the ESP32 module and the Graphical LCD. Therefore, this work presents a clear explanation of connecting the Graphical LCD to the ESP32 module using only three GPIO pins.

articleTitle: An Op-amp Sharing Folded Bernoulli Mapping TRNG for Low-power Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: An operational amplifier sharing (Op-amp sharing), folded Bernoulli mapping chaos-based true random number generator (TRNG) is proposed in this paper. Based on the concept of Op-amp sharing for non-flipped folded Bernoulli mapping, the number of stages is reduced from two stages to one, which reduces power consumption and improves the stability of the system. The entire system has been implemented in a standard 180nm process with power supply of 1.2V, and the output speed of random number is 400kbit/s with power consumption of only 21μW. The generated random bits pass National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Pub-800.22 randomness tests successfully.

articleTitle: A High Throughput QC-LDPC Decoder Architecture for Near-Earth Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper presents a high throughput decoder architecture for the (8176,7154) quasi-cyclic (QC) low density parity check (LDPC) code (C2) recommended by the Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS) for near-earth applications. The architecture avoids memory conflict through the use of multiple shift register based memory circuits and a pipe stage forwarding mechanism, thus allowing for heavy pipelining of the core processing unit. The decoder is implemented on the Xilinx XCVU9P FPGA platform and achieves a throughput of 2.65 Gbps at 10 iterations at a clock frequency of 253 MHz.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Modeling Method for Assembly Quality Control of Complex Products
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Digital twin technology can realize the integration and iterative optimization between the physical model and information model of complex products through real-time data collection, data integration and monitoring, thereby shortening the product development cycle and improving the product quality. Aiming at the problems of insufficient predictability of quality control in the assembly process of complex products, timeliness of quality control and weak systematicity, this paper applied the digital twin to the quality control of the complex products assembly process and analyzed the research progress of the digital twin technology. From the perspective of the whole process of product assembly, it discussed the information expression and model integration of the digital twin model of the assembly process and studied the typical characteristics of the digital twin model's multi-level and multi-dimensional and the modeling process of the model. The equipment, materials, process, environment, and other elements of the company are modeled, and the problem of the coordinated operation of multi-disciplinary models in the assembly process of complex products is solved by optimizing the model of the assembly quality control of complex products. A case verified the feasibility of the proposed digital twin modeling method.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of SimBlock to NS-3 Blockchain Simulators
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Blockchain is a technology that is in the hype and growing rapidly. Data that has entered the blockchain cannot be changed and tampered with, and this feature makes blockchain technology guaranteed in its integrity and security. However, evaluating a blockchain network configuration, consensus, design, or architecture has its problems due to the vast area of the blockchain network and the massive number of nodes. A simulator is the right choice for this case. Blockchain simulators that exist today include SimBlock and NS-3 blockchain simulator from Arthur Gervais. This study compares the two simulators' performance in terms of CPU, memory, and simulation time usage. Equalize all the two simulators' parameters, using the same configuration for the virtual machines used. After that, calculate the CPU and memory usage using the Sysstat program on Ubuntu, while the simulation time is taken from both simulator's output. This simulator evaluated by varying the target block from 500 to 5000 with 1000 nodes on the network. The experiment result of SimBlock CPU usage was ± 10% higher than NS-3, while SimBlock memory usage was also ± 14% greater than NS-3. The result of NS-3 simulation time requires the highest time of 55188.3s, while Simblock only takes 68.242s for the same number of blocks and nodes. The difference in CPU power is because NS-3 simulates the mining process. In contrast, the SimBlock mining process is not simulated but calculated using the user input value on the average mining power.

articleTitle: eSim: An Open Source EDA Tool for Mixed-Signal and Microcontroller Simulations
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: The ability to carry out simulations before making a PCB can save a lot of time, effort and cost. This work explains the creation of an open source mixed-signal simulation software eSim that will be of great help to students, hobbyists, the SME sector and startups. Analog and digital components are respectively modelled using SPICE and a hardware descriptive language in eSim. Inclusion of AVR based microcontroller as a part of the digital circuit is demonstrated through its instructions implemented as a C code library. This methodology could be used to provide support to other microcontroller families, such as PIC, STM and also more sophisticated controllers. These concepts are demonstrated through a few examples.

articleTitle: Modelingof the Effect of Skin Temperature on Hydration Assessment
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Bio-electrical impedance analysis (BIA) has high potentials to be used in assessing body composition due to it being non-invasive, easy to use, safe, and low-cost. To utilize its potentials, the effect of several parameters, such as electrode design, temperature, sweat, and body movement, must be studied to design a sensor that can be used in the field rather than in clinical settings. In this paper, a human skin model is developed and simulated to analyze the BIA method. The paper focused on studying the effect of temperature on the measured resistance and capacitance in relation to the hydration levels. The work presented can be used, in addition to future analysis, as a guideline to design a hydration assessment system.

articleTitle: A Capacitor-less LDO with Nested Miller Compensation and Bulk-Driven Techniques in 90nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper presents an output-capacitor-less low-dropout regulator (LDO) with nested miller compensation and bulk-driven techniques. The proposed LDO has been fabricated in TSMC 90 nm CMOS technology. The nominal supply voltage of the LDO is 1.8 V and the output voltage is 1.2 V. Bulk-driven technique is used to improve the power supply rejection Ratio (PSRR), which are -64 dB at 100 kHz and -24 dB at 25 GHz. It occupies 160 μm × 85 μm of chip area. Measurement results show the drop-out voltage is 200 mV at the maximum output current of 40 mA.

articleTitle: 110dB Ω, 336MHz Bandwidth, Low Noise Transimpedance Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper presents differential inputs to single ended output transimpedance amplifier (TIA) preceded by voltage amplifier and buffer to derive 1pF load. The main objective of this work is to achieve high trans-impedance gain while meeting other required performances. It is simulated in CMOS AMI Semiconductor’s C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> process. For frequency bandwidth extension (−3-dB BW), inductive-peaking technique is employed. The simulation results demonstrate that proposed design of TIA analog front end (TIA-AFE) achieves high transimpedance gain of 110dBΩ and −3-dB bandwidth of 336MHz for 50fF input capacitance. The input noise spectral density is about 1.6 pA/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> at frequency 336MHz. TIA consumes 21mW DC power under 5V supply voltage and this design is suitable for optical sensing receiver and other related applications.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network Accelerator Design for the Multi-task, High performance, and Energy-efficient Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: In recent years, Edge computing for AI applications has been the focus of research by various companies and academic units in order to achieve high speed real-time computations. Therefore, the submitted work separates the convolution operations so that the proposed accelerator can not only operate in the convolutional networks, but also operate in the lightweight neural networks. The main design focus is to utilize a tiled structure to optimize the suitable size resided in the block of input data. The proposed design also implements the data flow and parallelism analysis to minimize the access of the memory for the DNN hardware circuit and to achieve the high efficiency of the operation. The PE hardware utilization rate of 100% for different kernel sizes can be realized through the PE design and the reduced kernel size without accounting for the data loading time. The proposed accelerator is constituted with 32 MACs and internal logic of 450k gates by implemented in TSMC 40nm process. The simulated energy efficiency can reach to 213.3 GOPS/W while operating at 500MHz.

articleTitle: An Improvement of Network Routing Protocol with K-Means Clustering for Reactive Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are currently used in many areas for monitoring environmental parameters. It is usually deployed in hard-to-access areas and batteries cannot be replaced. WSN components must be designed for energy efficiency for both hardware and software. A routing protocol is needed to manage the network and help extend network lifetime. This work addresses the WSN protocol for reactive networks by aiming to develop a clustering method, which is a huge impact on energy consumption in the routing protocol. K-Means algorithm is deployed for efficiency sensor nodes clustering. The cluster head selection is done based on the maximum remaining energy node in each cluster. Simulation is performed to demonstrate the performance of the proposed scheme. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme has better performance than ordinary protocols and able to extend network lifetime. The characteristics of the proposed scheme are verified by using different sample datasets as well.

articleTitle: A Constant Potential Circuit for Electrochemical Detection of Tear Glucose
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Diabetes is a disease with high incidence rate and incurable disease. According to the research at home and abroad, there is a linear relationship between tear glucose and blood glucose. Therefore, this paper proposed a method to obtain the blood glucose concentration by measuring the tear glucose. A constant potential circuit based on electrochemical three-electrode system for detecting tear glucose concentration was designed. The circuit included voltage inverter, stabilized voltage, negative feedback and microcurrent amplification module. Multisim simulation results showed that the circuit had low noise and better amplification accuracy. The PCB test board was designed and processed by Altium Designer software. The output voltage of the circuit was 100mV up to 2300mV when detecting the glucose solution from 0.1~0.6mmol/L. The experimental results showed that the circuit could be applied in the electrochemical three- electrode system.

articleTitle: Ambient Light Suppression in Visible Light Transceivers: A Review
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Visible light communication has emerged as a promising complementary technology to enable communication between vehicles and traffic infrastructure. However, the visible light transceivers suffer from optical interference and ambient light saturation which severely affect the reception of the optical signal. In this paper, we present an overview of background light suppression techniques and analyse their merits and demerits. Mainly, the practical applicability of each technique for the integrated photodiode-based visible light receivers in automotive applications are discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: AL-MAC: Adaptive Error Compensation Approximate MAC
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Approximate calculation is extensively used in fault-tolerant applications as an extremely effective method of saving energy by balancing performance between accuracy and power consumption. Herein, an adaptive error compensation approximate multiplication and accumulation (AL-MAC) based on the logarithmic principle is proposed, which takes two factors into account. (a) LFC (leftmost-one filtering circuit) extracts the valid bits of the input data for calculation, thus reducing the circuit power consumption and area caused by unnecessary level flipping; (b) ACC (adaptive compensation circuit) conducts the adaptive error compensation, which is compensated according to the error distribution regulation. The evaluation results show that the proposed AL-MAC can save 33.8% of the power consumption and 19.38% of the area in a processing element of the neural network hardware accelerator compared with the standard exact MAC. Moreover, it has good performance on image processing.

articleTitle: Core–shell Ag@TiO2 Nanowire Network Based Volatile Threshold Resistive Switching Device
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: In core-shell nanowire (NW) networks, the electrical connectivity of nanoscale core-shell nanowire junction can be modulated for potential applications in modern electronic components, especially the resistive switching (RS) application. In this work, an Ag@TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> core-shell structure was deliberately designed to fabricate a resistive switching device with an Ag/Ag@TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/Ag planar structure, in which the Ag core can act as metallic interconnect and the insulating TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> shell acts as a switching medium to provide a conductive pathway for Ag filament migration. The device displays a volatile threshold resistive switching characteristic, and an on/off ratio of ~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> was achieved. This work provides a foundation for engineering core-shell Ag@TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanowire network for RS devices.

articleTitle: A 0.03-3GHz Wideband Inductorless Receiver in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: An inductorless wideband receiver supporting multiple wireless communication standards from 0.03GHz to 3GHz is presented in this paper. It adopts Low-Intermediate Frequency (IF) architecture. A two-stage inductorless wideband low noise amplifier (LNA), with Capacitor Cross Coupling (CCC) technique at the common gate stage and Multiple Gated Transistors (MGTR) technique at both common gate and common source stages, is proposed in Radio Frequency (RF) front end. Impedance translation structure is introduced for suppressing the blocking signal. A three-stage sub Biquads low-pass filter (LPF) is designed to enhance the stopband rejection performance. Single miller feed-forward compensation is introduced in its transimpedance amplifier (TIA) design as well for the sake of power saving. This wideband receiver is fabricated in standard 65nm RFCMOS process, occupying 3.9mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The whole receiving chain achieves a maximum link gain of 104.53dB and a minimum single sideband noise figure (SSB NF) of 6.809dB in simulation. When the receiver is in 3GHz frequency band and the bandwidth of LPF is about 20MHz, the in-band and out-of-band input third-order intercept point are -27.186dBm/-20.8761dBm, respectively. The core circuit consumes 99-104mW under 1.2V/2.5V supply.

articleTitle: A 7/27GHz Dual-Band Phase-Controlled Oscillator for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, a unique structure 7/27GHz dual-band voltage control oscillator (VCO) using oscillator mode reusing technology is designed, implemented and verified in a standard 90nm CMOS technology for 5G low and medium band applications. The dual-band VCO achieves more than three times band space thanks to the unique structure of inductor using two magic couple field. The mode switcher is also carefully design for lower noise and band switching loss. Mode switching avoids current-source switching resulting in long VCO setup time, which achieves a fast band switch. The measured phase noise of proposed dual-band VCO are -112.5 and -100dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset at 7.4GHz and 27.1GHz respectively, while only costuming 6.6mW at 0.5V supply, which make it suitable for low-power mobile communication applications. The proposed dual-band oscillator core occupies a chip area of 0.28mm*0.28mm without testing pads.

articleTitle: A Clock Generation Module Covering 500MHz to 12GHz for Sub-6GHz 5G Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: A clock generation module, consisting of two voltage controlled oscillators (VCO) and two triplers, is proposed. As one of the most critical components in sub-6GHz 5G wireless transceivers [1], the clock generation circuit is required to have wide tuning range and low phase noise. The key design details of the module including VCO and tripler are discussed. Two techniques are adopted to improve the performance of the self-mixing tripler. The first technique is to use triple stacked structure to reuse current and reduce power consumption and area; the second is to use a 90° phase difference delay locked loop (DLL) to suppress the output fundamental component. The clock generation module has been fabricated in a 28nm process and partially verified by measurements. According to the simulation and measurement results, the clock generation module can cover the frequency range from 500MHz to 12GHz. The phase noise of the high band VCO is -128 dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset at max frequency with a FOM of 188dB; The average output power of tripler is 1dBm and the output range is from 4.5GHz to 12.6GHz. The clock generation module can meet the requirement of sub-6GHz 5G wireless application.

articleTitle: An 8 bit to 12 bit Resolution Programmable 5 MSample/s Current Steering Digital-to-Analog Converter in a 22 nm FD-SOI CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: We present a 5 MSample/s current steering digital-to-analog converter which has a programmable resolution between 8 bit, 10 bit and 12 bit. A selectable 2-D unary matrix architecture and a resolution programmable decoder are proposed for the resolution programmability. The proposed current steering digital-to-analog converter is implemented in a 22 nm FD-SOI (Fully Depleted Silicon-on-Insulator) CMOS technology. The simulation verifications of the CS-DAC at three resolution modes are made. The maximum DNL of 0.06 LSB is obtained at 8 bit resolution modes, and the maximum INL (Integral Non-Linearity) of 0.53 LSB is obtained at 12 bit resolution modes. The minimum SFDR (Spurious-Free Dynamic Range) of 47.93 dBc is obtained at 8 bit resolution mode.

articleTitle: Developing a Printed Respiration Rate Sensor for E-textile Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Real-time monitoring of the vital signs in everyday life enables early detection of various diseases and disorders that can cause a life-threatening incident. In this paper, a biocompatible strain sensor for real-time monitoring of the human respiration rate is proposed. The sensor consists of a stretchable fabric substrate impregnated with carbon black through drop-casting at ambient conditions. The proposed passive sensor provides a change in electrical resistance from 160 Ω down to 80 Ω against applied tensile strain 0 % to 16 %. Electrical resistance of the sensor decreases due to shrinkage of the conducting yarns and resets to the initial resistance value when released with the help of Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) encapsulation elastomeric properties and fabric’s stretchability. The resistance variation phenomenon is exploited for the respiration rate detection application. The sensor is characterized for electrical and mechanical properties. The proposed sensor can be a good candidate for the respiration rate monitoring in E-textile and wearable electronics.

articleTitle: A Millimeter Wave Class-F VCO with Third Harmonic Enhancement in 40nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, the proposed millimeter-wave voltage controlled oscillator (VCO) is based on Class-F oscillator and adopts the design of multi-peak transformer to enhance the third harmonic so as to obtain higher frequency and lower phase noise. A high frequency millimeter wave VCO is realized by the design of a low frequency resonator. As a result, the VCO has lower phase noise and lower power consumption while obtaining wider frequency tuning range than traditional mm-Wave VCOs. In addition, a broadband buffer with a low-k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> transformer which can suppress the first-harmonic and extract the third-harmonic is proposed. Simulated results show that the proposed VCO exhibits phase noise of -93.6~-95.1dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset at 72.8~90.1 GHz, and the DC power consumption of the VCO core is only 10.8mW at the supply voltage of 0.9V.

articleTitle: Prediction of Heart Rate and Blood Oxygen from Physiological Signals
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Wearable sensors have received massive interest from the research community due to their usage in a variety of applications. Particularly, great efforts have been oriented to non-invasive health monitoring of humans with the help of wearable sensors. For non-invasive health monitoring, a wide range of sensors is being developed and used. Among these sensors, some are more difficult to build and wear as compared to others. Blood Oxygen level and Heart Rate monitoring sensors, for instance, are among those sensors which are not easy to build and wear on the body continuously. In this paper, we present a novel idea of predicting blood oxygen level and heart rate from other physiological signals of easy to build and wear sensors like temperature, electrodermal activity, and acceleration. A state-of the-art supervised learning method called Random Forest is used to train and test the model on a publicly available dataset. The proposed method is also compared with several baseline regression techniques like KNN, and Support Vector regressor. Our proposed method achieved 0.9494 coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and 3.26 root mean squared error for heart rate prediction. Whereas, a root mean squared error of 0.5589 and an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.8565 for the prediction of blood oxygen was achieved.

articleTitle: A 10-bit Pulse Width Modulation Based Analog to Digital Converter
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: A 10-bit pulse width modulated analog to digital converter (ADC) is proposed in this paper. The ADC is based on simple analog blocks and designed to operate as a back-end digital interface for sensor readout circuits. Our design incorporates simple blocks such as a chopped comparator and a 10-bit digital counter with few switches and passive elements to implement a very functional and versatile ADC for bridge readout circuits. Designed and simulated in 0.18µm CMOS process, the ADC consumes 55µA supply current and achieves an linearity of around 9-bits without any jitter compensation. The simulated DNL error is less than ±1 LSB for this ADC.

articleTitle: Slanted PVA/AA-Based Transmission Volume Holographic Gratings
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: The design of transmission volume holographic gratings was proposed in this work. The PVA/AA-based dry photopolymeric material was prepared as holographic recording media. The optical setup using to prepare the volume holographic gratings was built up. Considering the spatial resolution of the photopolymer dry film, the gratings with different spatial frequencies were prepared and the diffraction efficiency of the waveguide structure was measured indirectly. The gratings with the max diffraction efficiency of 44.92% was demonstrated. The holographic waveguide was fabricated with the grating with the optimized diffraction efficiency as an input coupler. The input of laser beam into the waveguide was realized with the designed structure.

articleTitle: Gate Current Cancellation Using a Replica PMOS and Digital Feedback for Temperature-coefficient Reduction on an Ultra-low Power Voltage Reference
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: A method to cancel the gate current loading at the output of ultra-low power voltage references using a replica PMOS and digital feedback is proposed, reducing the achieved temperature coefficient (TC). A time-based ultra-low power gate current-to-digital circuit, which takes advantage of an inherently infinite current-controlled oscillator (CCO)-based integrator gain to sense picoamperes of gate current, and an intrinsically low-bandwidth sensed gate current, is implemented. In addition, the practical and the fundamental limitation on the maximum achievable resolution of the gate current sensor is derived. Furthermore, a new figure of merit (FOM) for ultra-low power voltage references is proposed, which considers not only their power consumption and TC, but also the value of its load current.

articleTitle: An Integration of Personal Health Device and HL7 FHIR Using CoAP
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: In the field of health care, various electronic instruments are applied. These devices have different types of data formats depending on the service provider. For this work, the integration of IoT technology and electronic health record system is proposed where HL7 FHIR standard and CoAP protocol are selected to overcome this problem. The communication protocols for IoT including CoAP and MQTT were compared in terms of data transfer package size and Round Trip Time (RTT). The experimental result shows that RTT of CoAP smaller than RTT of MQTT while the packages of CoAP are smaller than MQTT as expected. We can see that the proposed system with HL7 FHIR can create a system interconnect between personal health devices and databases seamlessly. The proposed system can apply to various applications of the health care domain.

articleTitle: Modular Class-AB Current Multiplier Based on Fully-Differential Hyperbolic Transconductor
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper presents a new class-AB current multiplier using fully differential hyperbolic sine transconductors based on floating-gate transistors. The proposed multiplier is developed from a hyperbolic sine multiplication identity which inherently provides a class-AB operation. The proposed multiplier was designed using 0.35 μm AMS CMOS process. Simulation results show that the proposed multiplier achieves -30 dB THD for high input modulation index of 23 while utilizing power consumption of 60 nW under a supply voltage of 3 V.

articleTitle: Sensors on Nonconventional Substrates Developed through Printing Technologies
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper presents the development of sensors on nonconventional substrates realized through the fast emerging printing technologies. Drop-on-demand inkjet, screen printing and aerosol jet printing are the leading rapid manufacturing techniques. The functional nanomaterials in their solution form are used for patterned deposition in a single pass making the process simple and very cost-effective. The patterned deposition and deterministic placement of various functional materials ranging from conducting, semiconducting and insulators are central to the development of a wide range of sensing devices. These devices being developed on nonconventional substrates particularly made from polymeric materials are playing significant role in advancements of printed wearable sensors and transducers. Here in this paper, we summarize some of our recent developments made towards realizing sensors on multiple substrates. A particular focus is oriented towards printing technologies for developing sensors in various geometric configurations. Also, few of the challenges faced by printing technologies are highlighted.

articleTitle: Research on the Cooperative and Optimal Scheduling Strategy of Multi-energy Demand Response Based on Cloud-Edge Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: The demand response under multi-energy interaction is no longer limited to load shedding or shifting, but should also include demand transformation between multiple energy types. The interaction is also no longer limited to the traditional two-way interaction between power companies and customers, but all entities that can provide or use other forms of energy become "third parties" in the interaction system of the integrated energy system. To address the problem of insufficient interaction between energy supply and demand in an integrated energy scenario, this paper establishes an optimal operation model that takes into account energy storage devices, energy coupling devices, and distributed renewable energy generation in the context of demand response by multiple energy aggregators, and solves for an optimal economic dispatch strategy. The simulation results of the algorithm prove that the strategy has good advantages in reducing the dispatching cost.

articleTitle: Effect of Ag2O Doping on the H2S Gas Sensing Properties of WO3 Nanosensor
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper we report the synthesis and characterization of tungsten oxide doped silver oxide nanostructures. The effect of silver doping on the optical and sensing properties of tungsten doped silver oxide is studied and characterized for low-temperature H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>S gas detection. Furthermore, we investigated the sensor response, electrical characteristics, response time of tungsten oxide (WO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) and tungsten oxide doped with silver oxide (Ag<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O/ WO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) at different concentrations at 25°C. The study also presents the influence of the silver oxide doping of WO3 on the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>S based sensors performance in terms of sensitivity and response time. The obtained results proved the possibility of synthesizing tungsten oxide-based gas sensors for future H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>S sensor devices. UV-VIS results reveal that doping WO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> with Ag<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O enhanced the absorption of WO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> in the visible region which is indicated in the red shift. Furthermore, the sensing properties of WO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> is increased compared to bare WO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and Ag<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O which shoed no response to H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>S in this temperature range. The electrical properties of WO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> also becomes ohmic as a result of Ag<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O doping. The study illustrates a good way to improve the gas sensors performance through Ag<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O doping.

articleTitle: Research on Sensorless Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Adaptive Sliding Mode Observer
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive feedback gain sliding mode observer is designed to solve the chattering and low speed problems of traditional sliding mode observer. By introducing the feedback value of extended back electromotive force into the current observation equation and reasonably designing the adaptive rate, the sliding mode observer can obtain better low-speed performance. At the same time, it is convenient to design the sliding mode gain and avoid the serious problem of low-speed chattering caused by excessive gain value. On the other hand, in order to suppress chattering of sliding mode observer, saturation function is used instead of symbol function as switch control function. In order to solve the phase delay problem caused by low-pass filter, a low-pass filter with variable cut-off frequency is designed. Finally, the effectiveness of the improved method is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of 3D Random Nanowire Network Based on Modified Kd-tree Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Random nanowire network has become an important material foundation of many emerging interdisciplinary subjects. In this study, a specific simulation method using kd-tree algorithm with scapegoat tree algorithm in 3D conductive nanowire network is proposed. This model differs from the traditional model based on kd-tree algorithm as the scapegoat tree algorithm is used to optimize the imbalance caused by kd-tree algorithm in the process of nanowire network generation to improve the efficiency of simulation. The results show the efficiency of the model with scapegoat tree algorithm is 1.2-1.4 times higher than that without scapegoat tree algorithm. In addition, the percolation characteristic is the basis of mechanical and electrical properties of nanowire networks which is greatly influenced by the volume fraction and the shape of conductive fillers in nanowire networks, therefore, the effects of volume fraction and aspect ratio (AR) of nanowires on the percolation probability of the network are investigated in our work. It finds that there is a nonlinear increasing trend of percolation probability with the increase of volume fraction of conductive nanowires, and a positive correlation between percolation probability and AR. The simulation results indicate that it is effective to obtain the percolation probability under different volume fraction and AR of conductive nanowires by using such simulation model based on the kd-tree algorithm modified by scapegoat tree algorithm.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Denoising Algorithm for Speckle Noise in DoFP Polarization Images
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive algorithm for filtering speckle noise in Division-of-Focal-Plane (DoFP) polarization images is presented. The proposed algorithm involves replacing the first round of operation in the Block-matching and 3D Filtering (BM3D) denoising algorithm with an adaptive thresholding technique based on the smoothness of an image patch. This improves the "Semi-Filtered" image that is passed to the final BM3D denoising round. With this adaptive technique, key image details are preserved and speckle noise is significantly suppressed. Experimental results on four DoFP test images indicate the significant performance of the proposed algorithm in suppressing speckle noise. This significant performance is then compared with the performance of other existing denoising algorithms. Comparison is done numerically using Peak-Signal-to-Noise-Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity (SSIM) Index scores. Thereafter, comparison is extended to visual results to ascertain agreement between the two sets of comparisons.

articleTitle: Study on Percolation State and Electrical Properties of Carbon Nanotube Network
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are often used as conductive fillers for nanocomposites thanks to their excellent electrical conductivity and high aspect ratio. Percolation probability and electrical conductivity are important parameters to measure the electrical properties of CNT network. In this work, a simulation model using Monte Carlo method in CNT network is proposed to study the effects of volume fraction and aspect ratio of CNTs on the percolation probability and electrical conductivity. The Monte Carlo method was introduced to simulate the random distribution of CNTs in the generation domain. It finds that the variation trends of percolation probability and electrical conductivity show a nonlinear rise with the increase of volume fraction of CNTs. Moreover, the network composed of CNTs with large aspect ratio can present percolation faster and reach saturation state earlier. Compared with a network formed by CNTs at aspect ratio of 80 in which percolation occurs at volume fraction of 2%, a network formed by CNTs at aspect ratio of 150 begins to percolate at volume fraction of 0.7%. The simulation results indicate that the simulation model based on Monte Carlo method can reflect the percolation state and electrical properties of CNT network and analyze the effects of volume fraction and aspect ratio on the percolation probability and electrical conductivity of CNT network quantitatively.

articleTitle: Low-Power High-Speed 8-bit Conditional Carry Adder (CCA) using Memristor Logic
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Memristive frameworks or Memristors have obtained significant consideration due to the universality and high-speed performances, low- energy consumption to expedite data processing in real-time. This article consolidates the use of memristor for the implementation of digital logic gates, such as AND, OR and XOR. By employing memristor-based logic gates with reduced transistor counts, high-performance 8-bit Conditional Carry Adder (CCA) configuration is realized for low-power arithmetic systems. Memristor based 2×1 multiplexer is proposed utilizing Cadence Virtuoso environment of GPDK 90nm CMOS technology. In terms of power and energy-delay product, 54.64% - 96.56% and 78.37% - 99.71% improvement is observed by analyzing with the earlier reported works. By considering fixed 1V supply voltage, the power matrices for the configuration is achieved using Spectre simulation. Finally, a 16-bit CCA configuration is realized using 8-bit CCAs.

articleTitle: Local Active Sub-Threshold Transconductance Enhancement Compensation for Three-Stage Amplifiers with Heavy Capacitance Loads
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: A local active sub-threshold transconductance enhancement compensation technique is proposed for driving ultra-large capacitive loads (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>). The sub-threshold transconductance enhancement compensation is used in outer loop of amplifier to enhance the cascode Miller compensation effect. At the same time, the local active compensation network is introduced to accurately eliminate the first pole-zero pair and improves the circuit stability. A new slew rate enhancement structure is also proposed, which can effectively increase the output swing. Implemented in standard 0.18-μm CMOS technology, proposed amplifier only consumes 41.27 μW of power at 1.2 V supply when driving a 20nF C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>, achieving a gain-bandwidth product of 3.02 MHz, a phase margin of 69°, and an average slew rate of 0.09V/μs. The capacitance of compensation is only 475 fF, and the chip area of entire amplifier is 0.0043mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Research on Single-Event Vulnerability and Hardening for a Pipelined ADC
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Analog to digital converters (ADCs) are ubiquitously required in modern spaceborne electronic systems. However, as a continually shrink of the technology feature sizes, single-event effects (SEEs) such as single-event transients (SETs) and single-event upsets (SEUs) can significantly cause performance degradation of the data converters exposed to radiation environments. This paper analyzes SE vulnerability in pipelined ADC. Circuit-level radiation-hardened-by-design (RHBD) techniques for analog SET (ASET) and a system-level digital calibration method for radiation hardening are discussed. Based on the dual-path technique, a prototype radiation hardened 14-bit 1GSPS pipelined ADC based on 65nm CMOS process is designed. Simulation results show a SFDR value of 79.91dB for a 1.7V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P-P</inf> 340.3MHz input sine wave at a sampling frequency of 1GHz with radiation immunity.

articleTitle: Heart Rate Classification Using TSTDP with BCM Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Bio signal processing requires a highly energy efficient and accurate computing hardware especially if the processing is done on-the-fly. Most of these requirements are very well met by neuromorphic principles. Detection and analysis are the two key stages of any bio signal analyzers. This paper is focused on the analysis part of the pipeline by proposing an algorithm to classify an Electrocardiogram (ECG) signal based on heart rate using Triplet Spike Timing Dependent Plasticity (TSTDP) learning rule whose parameters have been tuned to obtain Bienenstock-Cooper-Munro (BCM) characteristics. The significance of BCM in rate-based signal processing is clearly highlighted in the proposed algorithm. Floating point algorithm has been proposed and used to implement TSTDP algorithm on digital hardware. The proposed work has an average classification accuracy of 96.5 % and is also efficiently realizable on digital hardware. The ECG datasets have been taken from PhysioBank ATM. The entire digital hardware design is done in VHDL and synthesis tool used is Xilinx Vivado. The targeted FPGA is Xilinx Spartan-7.

articleTitle: Study on Electro-Optical Control Performance of Holographic Polymer Dispersed Liquid Crystal Grating
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Compared with ordinary volume holographic gratings, holographic polymer dispersed liquid crystal(H-PDLC) grating has the advantage of adjustable electronically controlled diffraction efficiency. In this work, we theoretically simulated the degree of refractive index modulation that affects the diffraction efficiency of holographic volume gratings. Through the interference of two symmetric laser beams, a symmetric transmission H-PDLC grating was made. The diffraction properties and electro-optical characteristics of the H-PDLC were also studied. Relevant experiments were conducted to prepare a volume holographic grating with a diffraction efficiency of 74.4% and a control amplitude of when an external 50Hz rectangular wave voltage of 40V/um was applied.

articleTitle: DDS-Based Analog IC Test System for Audio ICs
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: IC testing has become an important supporting technology for the IC industry. A comprehensive and rigorous IC test process can not only improve the reliability of the products, but also reduce costs. In this work, a home-made analog IC test system was developed based on direct digital synthesis (DDS) and field programmable gate array (FPGA) that specialized in manufacturing testing for ETEK audio analog devices including audio DAC, audio effect processing circuit, and audio power amplifier circuit. Such system is cost-efficient and function-trimmed so as to lower the cost while still satisfying the basic needs of audio analog testing. In this article, the hardware design and implementation of such home-made analog IC test system was described and illustrated. The validity of such system was shown by the result of a trial-run test from a batch of audio power amplifiers, and the comparison of the obtained parameters with those from the commercial system further verified that our design and implementation of IC test system could be well adopted in the industry for manufacturing testing.

articleTitle: Real-Time Deep Neuro-Vision Embedded Processing System for Saliency-based Car Driving Safety Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Recently, much interest has been aroused by scientific community regarding visual saliency-based applications. The proposed approach contributes to the progressive growth of knowledge of video saliency applications in the automotive field. Through the visual saliency detection, the car driver assistance systems (ADAS i.e. Advanced Driver Assistance Systems) are able to process the driving observation scene selectively. Specifically, it has been observed that the drivers along the driving route, focuses his/her gaze on some objects rather than others. This is determined by the perceptual activity of the brain which through the visual saliency determine the focused scene. We propose a driving safety assessment pipeline which combines a near-real time drowsiness car driver monitoring system driven by a visual saliency detection applied to the acquired driving scene. The proposed approach includes ad-hoc 3D pre-trained Semantic Segmentation Deep Network combined with ad-hoc 1D temporal Deep Dilated Convolutional Neural Network. This architecture was developed for the embedded platform based on STA1295 Accordo5 core (ARM A7 Dual-Cores) embedding an hardware graphics accelerator. The proposed system embeds a bio-sensor which will be placed on the steering wheel of the car having the target to collect the driver's Photoplethysmography (PPG) signal and which will result in a control of driver attention level. The so collected PPG time-series will be classified by the mentioned 1D Temporal Deep Convolutional Network which provides an assessment of the driver attention level. A final analyzer block verifies if the car driver attention level is adequate for the saliency-based scene classification. The performed tests confirmed the effectiveness of the overall proposed pipeline.

articleTitle: Hybrid PSO-GWO Optimization Based Parameter Extraction Method Applied to GaN Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: In this research, four different equivalent circuit models that characterize the substrate/buffer loading effect for GaN HEMT on Si substrate have been investigated. Z-parameter measurements of an open de-embedded structure have been used to characterize this effect in 16×200 μm GaN HEMT on Si. An optimization technique based on hybridization between two meta-heuristic techniques which are Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) has been developed to extract the models' elements. Each of those techniques has been tested separately to evaluate the performance of the proposed technique. The validation process of the extracted elements is done by comparing the simulated and the measured data of the model. The accuracy and the rate of convergence of the extraction results are considered as evaluation criteria. The proposed PSO-GWO technique shows a very good agreement with previous research results, which accordingly validates the applicability of this technique for small- and large-signal modeling of transistors.

articleTitle: Verification of Open-Source Memory Compiler Framework with a Practical PDK
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: An open-source memory compiler has recently drawn the attention of academic researchers involved in Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) designs. Since simulation results for circuits implemented by practical Process Design Kits (PDKs) have rarely been reported so far, the effectiveness and the reliability for circuit implementation by compiler still needs to be further verified. This paper presents an SRAM circuit implemented in a 0.6μm/±2.5V CMOS process with the compiler framework. We present pre- and post-layout simulation results with respect to the functionality and various performance parameters of our SRAM circuit, and the simulation results are thoroughly analyzed. A summary for our SRAM circuit demonstrates the effectiveness and the reliability of the compiler to design an SRAM in a fabricable technology process, showing a promising result for the compiler to be verified on a fabricated chip.

articleTitle: Substation Switch State Recognition Method Based on NSST Image Fusion
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: In view of the problem of misjudgment of switch state image recognition in substation, this paper proposes a method of substation switch image recognition based on the Non-Subsampled Shearing Transform (NSST) image fusion. According to their characteristics and complementary relationship, the visible image and infrared image are fused based on the NSST image fusion algorithm, and the fused image containing rich details and contour features of the two switch source images is generated. The improved Speeded Up Robust Features (SURF) algorithm is used to extract and match the target features of the fusion image, and then the multi threshold image segmentation technology based on the Chaotic Cuckoo Search (CCS) algorithm is used for processing. Finally, the slope of the line where the switch arm and two contacts are located is obtained based on Hough transform, and the switch state is judged according to the angle difference between them. Simulation results show the reliability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Integrated Fall Prevention System with Single-Channel EEG and EMG Sensor
publicationTitle: 2021 4th International Conference on Circuits, Systems and Simulation (ICCSS)
abstract: Falls are the leading cause of injury and death in the global population, it is a major concern for home-alone elderly. The proposed system aims to provide a low-cost EEG and EMG-based fall prevention system by providing real-time feedback to the user. At the front end, a single EEG electrode placed at Cz position is used to detect movement intention by extracting the Movement Related Cortical Potential (MRCP) patterns in real-time, experimental results showed 83.3% accuracy. Upon the detection of MRCP, the system will send a cue to the EMG sensor, and the user's EMG reading will be analysed and compared against the pre-characterized user profile. A match filter is used to determine whether the subject is fit to move or should stop moving. This process will be completed within 500ms and would leave enough time to alert the user should the system determine that the muscle state of the user is weaker than normal since MRCP typically occurs 1.5 seconds before the actual movement. The EMG match filter has an accuracy of 80%. In addition, a real-time posture detection utilizing supervised machine learning was also incorporated to realize continuous monitoring for unbalanced conditions when the user is moving. For classification, the K-nearest neighbours (KNN) classifier was chosen for a good accuracy result. It is able to identify stationary, walking, and unbalanced walking states. The accuracy rate for the KNN model is 89%.
